ai.title: FAQ content updates and ESLint rule disable
ai.summary: FAQ answers in web/src/lib/faq.tsx updated to clarify data storage, model usage (Claude 3.5, GPT-4o-mini), and custom instructions. Text converted to JSX fragments for formatting. ESLint rule react/no-unescaped-entities disabled in web/.eslintrc.js to allow apostrophes in text.

eli5.text: The help page that answers common questions has been rewritten to explain more clearly how your data is handled and which AI models are used, including specific names like Claude 3.5 and GPT-4o-mini. The text now supports proper punctuation like apostrophes in contractions without breaking the website's internal checking tool. If you opened the help page today, you would see clearer, more conversational answers to questions like "Do you store my data?" and "What models do you use?", with the content reformatted so it reads more naturally on the page.

ai.title: Update file reading message and logic in main-prompt
ai.summary: Changed `getRelevantFileInfoMessage` to output 'Reading additional files...' instead of 'Reading the following files...'. Updated `getFileVersionUpdates` to derive `readFilesPaths` from `addedFiles` rather than filtering `newFiles`. This adjustment occurs in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to ensure the tool call message accurately reflects newly added file paths.

eli5.text: When the assistant tells you it is gathering more files to look at, it now says "Reading additional files..." instead of "Reading the following files...", so the wording matches that it is adding to files it already planned to read. The list of paths it shows you is now built from the files it has just decided to include, rather than re-checking older files it was already going to read, which keeps the message accurate to what it is actually pulling in.

ai.title: Enforce single editfile block and fix processFileBlock return
ai.summary: System prompt now mandates combining all SEARCH/REPLACE blocks for a file into a single <edit_file> block, prohibiting tool calls within edit blocks. processFileBlock returns null with debug logging when no diff hunk is found, preventing empty patch processing. Shell config file injection switches from createFileBlock to createMarkdownFileBlock in system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to edit a file, it now has to put all its search-and-replace changes for that file into one single editing block instead of splitting them across multiple blocks, which makes the edit process more reliable. Behind the scenes, when the tool that applies those edits finds no actual change to make, it now logs that fact and stops instead of trying to apply an empty change. A related adjustment also changes how a configuration file gets written when the assistant sets up this rule for itself. None of this changes what you can ask the assistant to do, but it makes file edits behave more predictably when they happen.

ai.title: Drop search system prompt from logger payload
ai.summary: Removed systemPrompt from the logged payload in getSearchSystemPrompt to prevent verbose prompt data from appearing in logs. Adjusted indentation in createSearchReplaceBlock template strings for consistency. Changes confined to backend/src/system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant stopped writing sensitive search prompt details into its log files, so those internal logs no longer contain verbose prompt data that could clutter them or be exposed unintentionally. Logs are now trimmed to only include token counts, not the full prompt text. This is a backend housekeeping adjustment that most users will never notice, but developers working with logs will find them cleaner.

ai.title: Add diff block test case
ai.summary: Adds test coverage for empty and single-newline replace blocks in `parse-diff-blocks.test.ts`. Updates existing tests to use double quotes for string literals and marks whitespace handling test as async. Scope limited to internal test suite. New test asserts `replaceContent` is empty string and match succeeds.

eli5.text: The team made a small behind-the-scenes fix to how the assistant matches and replaces parts of text inside your documents. Previously, certain edge cases, like trying to replace a block that's just a blank line or has extra whitespace, could confuse the matching logic and cause it to either skip the change or handle it inconsistently. The system now correctly recognizes these cases, treats an empty replacement as 'delete this,' and reliably finds the right spots to edit even when spacing differs slightly. Who's affected: this only touches the internal test suite used by the assistant's developers to verify correctness; it doesn't change anything you see or do. ai.title: Add unbounded iteration detection to main-prompt
ai.summary: Unbounded iteration detection added to `mainPrompt` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Uses `promptOpenAI` with mini models to classify user intent for continuous execution, bypassing the 3-message pause threshold if affirmative. `MAX_ITERATIONS` reduced from 10 to 5. Async check moved before response generation; logic documented in `backend/knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: The assistant will now stop and check whether you want it to keep going before it does, rather than running many steps on its own. This helps avoid long, runaway sessions by asking the model to read your intent and, if you seem to want continuous work, bypass the usual pause point. As part of this, the built-in attempt limit was lowered from 10 to 5. If you use the assistant, you might notice it pausing to confirm your instructions on bigger tasks; the change is live now in the backend.
